"""Command-line interface: ``stockctl list|low|summary FILE``."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence

from stockctl.filters import SORT_KEYS, by_location, low_items, sort_items
from stockctl.items import ItemError, read_items
from stockctl.report import format_list, format_low, format_summary
from stockctl.stats import summarize


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """The argument parser for the three commands."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="stockctl", description="Stock lists from a warehouse CSV export."
    )
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    listing = commands.add_parser("list", help="print every item")
    listing.add_argument("file", help="CSV export of the warehouse system")
    listing.add_argument("--location", help="only items stored at this location")
    listing.add_argument("--sort", choices=SORT_KEYS, default="sku", help="order of the lines")

    low = commands.add_parser("low", help="print the items to reorder")
    low.add_argument("file", help="CSV export of the warehouse system")
    low.add_argument("--location", help="only items stored at this location")

    summary = commands.add_parser("summary", help="print totals")
    summary.add_argument("file", help="CSV export of the warehouse system")
    return parser


def _fail(message: str) -> int:
    print(f"stockctl: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 2


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run the command line; returns the exit status (2 for unreadable input)."""
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        items = read_items(args.file)
    except ItemError as exc:
        return _fail(str(exc))
    except OSError as exc:
        return _fail(f"cannot read {args.file}: {exc.strerror or exc}")

    if args.command == "list":
        chosen = sort_items(by_location(items, args.location), args.sort)
        sys.stdout.write(format_list(chosen))
    elif args.command == "low":
        sys.stdout.write(format_low(low_items(by_location(items, args.location))))
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(format_summary(summarize(items)))
    return 0

finish.thought: The parser raises it, the CLI prints it.
finish.report: The message comes from parse_items in src/stockctl/items.py. When a SKU shows up a second time it raises ItemError with the line of the second row and the text 'duplicate sku X (first on line N)', where N is the line of the first row. The CLI prints it as 'stockctl: line <second row>: duplicate sku ...' and exits with status 2. So the line number in the prefix is the second occurrence, the one to fix or remove, and the first occurrence is named inside the message.

"""Plain-text output for the stockctl commands."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence

from stockctl.items import Item
from stockctl.stats import Summary


def format_list(items: Sequence[Item]) -> str:
    """A table with one line per item."""
    if not items:
        return "(no items)\n"
    sku_w = max(len("SKU"), *(len(item.sku) for item in items))
    name_w = max(len("NAME"), *(len(item.name) for item in items))
    qty_w = max(len("QTY"), *(len(str(item.qty)) for item in items))
    lines = [f"{'SKU':<{sku_w}}  {'NAME':<{name_w}}  {'QTY':>{qty_w}}  LOCATION"]
    for item in items:
        lines.append(
            f"{item.sku:<{sku_w}}  {item.name:<{name_w}}  {item.qty:>{qty_w}}  {item.location}"
        )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def format_low(items: Sequence[Item]) -> str:
    """One line per low item, saying how far below the reorder level it is."""
    if not items:
        return "nothing to reorder\n"
    lines = [
        f"{item.sku}  {item.name}: {item.qty} left, reorder at {item.reorder_at}, "
        f"short by {item.short_by()}"
        for item in items
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def format_summary(summary: Summary) -> str:
    """The summary block."""
    lines = [
        f"items: {summary.items}",
        f"units: {summary.units}",
        f"low: {summary.low}",
        f"value: {summary.value}",
    ]
    lines.extend(f"  {name}: {units}" for name, units in summary.by_location.items())
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

finish.thought: Ordering is by shortage, then SKU.
finish.report: low_items in src/stockctl/filters.py keeps the items at or below their reorder level and sorts them by how many units they are short, the largest shortage first, with the SKU as the tie-breaker. An item with no reorder level (an empty reorder_at in the CSV) is never low, so it never appears in the low report. The text report prints one line per item with the quantity left, the reorder level, and the shortage.

"""Totals over a list of items."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import Decimal

from stockctl.items import CENT, Item


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Summary:
    """Totals for a stock list."""

    items: int
    units: int
    low: int
    value: Decimal
    by_location: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)


def summarize(items: Iterable[Item]) -> Summary:
    """Count items and units, the low items, the stock value, and units per location."""
    rows = list(items)
    per_location: dict[str, int] = {}
    for item in rows:
        per_location[item.location] = per_location.get(item.location, 0) + item.qty
    return Summary(
        items=len(rows),
        units=sum(item.qty for item in rows),
        low=sum(1 for item in rows if item.is_low()),
        value=sum((item.value() for item in rows), Decimal(0)).quantize(CENT),
        by_location=dict(sorted(per_location.items())),
    )
